Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, UnitedHealth Group, Qualcomm, Commonwealth Bank, and Mercor. Email, chat, tickets, documents, code, CRM and HR records are some of the most valuable training data left for AI labs, and almost none of it can change hands until the people in it are protected.
  
  
We sit between the company that owns the data and the lab that wants it, as the independent third party. We take in the corpus, find the people and organizations referenced across all of those systems, give each real identity one consistent synthetic replacement, rebuild every file in its original format, and deliver the result with a written report on how it was done. The data still reads like a company doing its work, which is what makes it worth training on.
  
  
**Why this role, why now**
Demand is running ahead of our capacity to deliver. Labs are buying, data owners are selling, and the buyers want datasets in days to weeks, not quarters. The technology can meet that timeline. What turns it into a delivered dataset is an engineer who can take a messy, half-documented corpus from a new client, get it through the pipeline, catch what breaks, and ship something both sides will sign off on.

* Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: documentation, runbooks, and improvements to the product.

**Your next job shouldn't be limited by your last job title.**

Some of the best engineers we've met didn't have the most impressive resumes. They weren't always at the most prestigious companies. They didn't necessarily have the right titles. Some were, some weren't, but that's not important.

What matters is give them something they'd never seen before, and they figured it out. Fast.

They asked better questions. They learned what they needed to learn. They weren't intimidated by problems they didn't immediately understand. And, importantly, they built things that worked.

**We're looking for more people like that.**

**The opportunity**

Peri is recruiting Forward Deployed Engineers for some of New York's most interesting AI startups, from Seed to Series D+, backed by investors including a16z, Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, and Y Combinator.

We've spent time with the founders, studied the people who are exceptional at these jobs, and learned what actually distinguishes them.

Here's what we've discovered:
**Ambition, curiosity, judgment, and the ability to learn quickly can matter a lot more than your current job title.**

You don't need to have been a Forward Deployed Engineer before. If you are currently then great. If not, keep reading.

**What you'll actually do**

Imagine walking into any type of business or company. You know almost nothing about how it works.

Your job is to figure it out. Talk to people. Understand how the business really operates. Find the problems worth solving. Then work with other engineers to build software that solves them.

You're part engineer, part detective, part operator.

You'll work directly with founders and senior executives. You'll own problems from the first conversation through deployment. And you'll see what happens when people actually use what you've built.

**These are roles for people who enjoy being thrown into the deep end.**

**Who we're looking for**

Maybe you're a software engineer who's always been more interested in the problem than the ticket you were assigned.

Maybe you've spent your career learning things you weren't supposed to know yet, taking on responsibilities you weren't technically qualified for, or figuring out how to do things nobody taught you.

**We care about all of that.**
But here's the catch.
**You have to help us see it.**

We can't tell from a resume how quickly you learn, how much initiative you take, or what happens when you're confronted with something completely unfamiliar.

So tell us. It doesn't need to be a heroic story. It needs to be real.

**Why aren't the company names listed?**

Because this isn't one anonymous job. We work with several companies looking for similar qualities in people, but offering different opportunities.

Rather than having you apply separately to half a dozen startups, we'd like to get to know you, understand what makes you unusually good at what you do, and figure out which opportunities might fit.

**We only work with companies we'd bet on ourselves.**

**Who is Peri?**

Most recruiting starts with a search: job title, company, school, years of experience.

We think that approach misses a lot of exceptional people.

So we start with the founders. We learn what makes someone successful at their company, then look for those qualities in people whose resumes may not tell the whole story.

We're particularly interested in people who are better than their credentials suggest.

**How to apply**

* Apply here and DM me on LinkedIn.
* No cover letter. No elaborate application.
* But we do want you to answer one question:
  **What's something you've figured out or built that makes you think you're capable of more than your resume suggests?**
* A few sentences are enough. Be specific. We're more interested in something real you've accomplished than how well you can sell yourself.
* If there's a potential fit, we'll have a conversation, tell you what we know about the companies, and help you understand which opportunities make sense. When there's a strong match, we can introduce you directly to the founders.

**And if you've read this far thinking, "I could be really good at this, but nobody would know it from my resume," we especially want to hear from you.**

**One last thing**

We take unconventional candidates seriously. That doesn't mean we're looking for people who aren't qualified to do the work.

If you're sitting at home mass-applying to every job you see without reading the description, can't demonstrate real engineering ability, have a fake or misleading LinkedIn profile, or aren't authorized to work in the United States,
**please don't apply
.**

**It's a waste of your time and ours.**

We're willing to look past credentials. We're not willing to look past a lack of effort, ability, or honesty.

**Surprise us with what you can do, not what you claim you can do.**
